_about: Why each class and relation exists, the alternatives considered, and who confirmed it. `validated_by` stays empty until a person who knows the domain has confirmed the entry.

Pursuit.question: Which opportunities are we pursuing with this client, at what stage, who leads each, and why did we win or lose?
Pursuit.why: A pursuit has its own dates, lead, documents and outcome before any engagement exists, and a lost pursuit never becomes one.
Pursuit.alternatives: A stage attribute on Engagement: rejected, because a lost pursuit would then be an engagement that never happened.

StatementOfWork.question: Is this request in scope under the signed SOW, and which clause says so?
StatementOfWork.why: Its signing date and clauses are what scope, pricing and key-person questions are judged against, so it must be addressable on its own.
StatementOfWork.alternatives: A document-kind attribute on Document: rejected, because questions need to ask for SOWs by type and traverse their scope.

ChangeOrder.question: What was the scope at signing compared with now, and why did each change happen?
ChangeOrder.why: Each change carries its own date, reason and value; without it the scope history collapses into the latest state.
ChangeOrder.alternatives: Superseding the SOW with a new version: rejected, because the reason and value of each change would be lost.

ScopeItem.question: Is this request in scope, and which clause says so?
ScopeItem.why: Scope is argued item by item and clause by clause; a scope paragraph on the SOW cannot answer which change added or removed a line.
ScopeItem.alternatives: Free text on the SOW: rejected, because it cannot say when an item entered or left scope.

SolutionDocument.question: Have we done work like this before, and which solution document can I reuse?
SolutionDocument.why: Reuse is the top need: solution documents must be findable by platform, regulation and problem, and carry their assumptions.
SolutionDocument.alternatives: Splitting proposals from solution documents: deferred until a question needs the difference.

Assumption.question: What does this solution assume about the client's environment, and which assumptions are still unconfirmed?
Assumption.why: An assumption is confirmed or invalidated on a date by someone, and an invalidated one is often the reason for a change order.
Assumption.alternatives: A list attribute on the solution document: rejected, because it would keep no confirmation or history.

PricingModel.question: Which pricing model is this engagement on, what sits behind the number, and is the margin inside the approved band?
PricingModel.why: A price is revised during a pursuit and by change orders; each revision keeps its margin and the decisions behind it.
PricingModel.alternatives: Price and model as attributes on Engagement: rejected, because revisions and exception approvals would have nowhere to attach.

MarginBand.question: Is the priced margin inside the approved band for its pricing model, and if not, who approved the exception?
MarginBand.why: The band is policy that changes over time; a price must be judged against the band in force when it was set.
MarginBand.alternatives: Constants in a rule: rejected, because the band changes and its history matters for past approvals.

Assignment.question: Who is staffed on this engagement, in which role, from when to when, and how does that compare with the plan?
Assignment.why: Staffing questions need person, role, engagement, dates and rates together, and plan and actual must sit side by side.
Assignment.alternatives: A direct person-to-engagement relation: rejected, because it holds no role, dates, allocation or rates.

Platform.question: Have we done work on this platform before, and who did it?
Platform.why: Platforms are shared across engagements and are the main way people search for similar past work.
Platform.alternatives: A tag attribute on Engagement: rejected, because free tags drift in spelling and cannot be traversed.

Regulation.question: Which regulations does this engagement touch, and what does that oblige us to do?
Regulation.why: Regulatory work is a main axis for finding past work and people, and obligations must trace to the instrument.
Regulation.alternatives: Regulatory categories (e.g. third-party risk): rejected as invented; cite the instrument instead.

Risk.question: What are the open risks and blockers, who owns each, and what are they waiting on?
Risk.why: A risk has an owner, a lifecycle and a dependency on someone; none of that fits on an action item or question.
Risk.alternatives: Reusing ActionItem: rejected, because a risk is a possibility to manage, not a task to finish.

Commitment.question: What did sales promise that delivery needs to know, and what has the client committed to provide and is any of it late?
Commitment.why: Promises in both directions have the same shape (who, what, by when, met or not); one class answers both.
Commitment.alternatives: Two classes, one per direction: rejected, because they would differ only in who made the promise.

BillingMilestone.question: Which milestones have been billed, and what can we bill this month?
BillingMilestone.why: A milestone has its own amount and due date and links acceptance of work to money.
BillingMilestone.alternatives: Amount attributes on Deliverable: rejected, because one milestone can cover several deliverables.

Invoice.question: Which invoices are outstanding?
Invoice.why: An invoice has its own number, amount, dates and state, separate from what it bills.
Invoice.alternatives: A billed flag on the milestone: rejected, because time-and-materials invoices have no milestone.

client_of.question: Which opportunities are we pursuing with this client?
client_of.why: Widened from the base to pursuits, so a client's pipeline and its engagements are read the same way.

owns.question: Who leads this pursuit, and who owns this risk?
owns.why: Widened from the base: leading a pursuit and owning a risk are the same accountability.
owns.alternatives: A separate led_by relation: rejected as a second word for the same thing.

decides.question: Who approved this price outside the margin band?
decides.why: Widened from the base so pricing exceptions and scope rulings are decisions with a date and a reason.
decides.alternatives: An approver attribute on the pricing model: rejected, because it keeps no reason or session.

became.question: What did sales promise that delivery needs to know on day one?
became.why: It is the handover: everything said during the pursuit stays reachable from the engagement.

solution_for.question: Which solution document can I reuse?
solution_for.why: Reuse needs to know what a solution was written for and how that turned out.

involves_platform.question: Have we done work on this platform before, and who did it?
involves_platform.why: Platform is the main way people search for similar past work and the people who did it.

subject_to.question: Which regulations does this engagement touch?
subject_to.why: The second search axis for similar work, and where obligations start.

assumes.question: What does this solution assume, and what is still unconfirmed?
assumes.why: Ties each assumption to what breaks if it proves false.

confirmed_by.question: Which assumptions are still unconfirmed?
confirmed_by.why: A confirmation with no source is just optimism.

amends.question: How has the scope changed since signing?
amends.why: A change order with no SOW is not a change to anything.

defines_scope.question: Is this in scope, and which clause says so?
defines_scope.why: Lets each scope item trace to the document and date that introduced it.

removes_scope.question: What was the scope at signing compared with now?
removes_scope.why: Removal is as much a scope change as an addition and needs its own record.
removes_scope.alternatives: Superseding the item: kept as well, but the change order must say it did it.

priced_by.question: Which pricing model is this engagement on?
priced_by.why: Links the commercial model to the work and its changes.

held_to.question: Is the priced margin inside the approved band?
held_to.why: The band in force at the time, not today's band, is what an approval was measured against.

staffs.question: Who is staffed on this engagement?
staffs.why: An assignment to nothing is not an assignment.

assignee.question: Who is staffed, and how does it compare with the plan?
assignee.why: Planned positions may be unnamed, so this is optional.

as_role.question: In which role, and at what rate?
as_role.why: Plan and actual are compared role by role.

worked_on.question: Who has done this kind of work before?
worked_on.why: The shortcut experience questions traverse; derived so nobody maintains it by hand.
worked_on.alternatives: A skills list per person: rejected, because self-declared skills drift from what people actually did.

key_person_for.question: Which commitments depend on one named person?
key_person_for.why: Key-person clauses and promises name individuals; roles cannot carry that risk.

signs_off.question: Which deliverables are waiting on sign-off, and who signs?
signs_off.why: Sign-off is distinct from ownership: the client signs what we own.

threatens.question: What are the open risks, and what do they threaten?
threatens.why: Ties a risk to the work and money at stake.

waits_on.question: What are the blockers waiting on?
waits_on.why: The person to chase is the answer people need from a blocker.

promised_by.question: What has the client committed to provide?
promised_by.why: Gives a commitment its direction without a second class.

commitment_for.question: What did sales promise during the pursuit?
commitment_for.why: Pre-sales promises must follow the pursuit into the engagement.

required_by.question: What does this regulation oblige us to do?
required_by.why: Obligations are traced to the instrument, never to an invented category.

sponsors.question: Who are our sponsors at this client, and how has that changed?
sponsors.why: Sponsors change; with roles and dated fills the history stays.

milestone_of.question: What can we bill this month?
milestone_of.why: A milestone belongs to one engagement or contract, which is where billing is reviewed.

bills_on.question: What can we bill this month?
bills_on.why: Billing follows acceptance; the link makes that readable.

invoices.question: Which invoices are outstanding, and for what?
invoices.why: An invoice must say what it bills, or it cannot be reconciled against milestones or time.
